promises.claim: A day you call in sick is left out of the attendance the review counts.
Once a run has had ${ESTIMATE.workNights} nights, the term’s review counts how they went.
The review counts the term’s coursework as shown: once ${ESTIMATE.coursework.shown} or more pieces are due, ${pct(ESTIMATE.coursework.unready)} or more Unready or not shown is short.
A review that finds you in good standing puts you back in the pool the chair casts from.
The review settles each course as passed, Incomplete or failed, and making up or repeating is how you put an Incomplete or a failed course right.
Each class grows its skills, and some of the abilities they’re related to.
How rested you come sets how much a class grows you.
Condition under ${ESTIMATE.sickBelow}, the flu or a limiting injury is what lets you call in.
An excused day is left out of the attendance the term’s review counts.
Each meeting missed ill stays on the course’s record as excused, and enough of them make it Incomplete.
A Saturday shift that day is excused when it comes, and its hours can be converted to grant aid.
Missing most of a term’s class days ill brings Yale Health’s assessment, which can end in a medical leave.
A rehearsal call that day is excused when it comes, and the blocking set without you is still there to catch up on from the book.
A rehearsal booked with a classmate that day is excused when it comes, and costs none of their trust.
Until you’re registered, every class day counts as an unexcused absence.
Work-study’s I-9 is done at registration. Unregistered, a shift is missed and can’t be converted.
You can’t ask a classmate you haven’t met to rehearse, and meeting your class meets them all.
The tour opens the studios and the library, and the courses session sets your first work.
Each session is on your calendar, and the clock stops at it.
A personal leave ends Yale Health’s student cover, and Affiliate cover keeps it.
A leave begun mid-term charges part of the term’s living-expense scholarship back to your Yale account.
Without notice of return by its date, the leave ends in dismissal.
Courses left on a leave stay on your record as Left On Leave, and you take them again when you’re back.
A medical leave needs a reason a physician would see, and coming back needs condition ${ESTIMATE.sickBelow} or more.
On an F-1, a medical leave extends the I-20 a year once it begins, and withdrawing leaves a grace period of ${STATUS_GRACE_DAYS.withdrawn} days and no OPT.
A leave ends the term’s castings and any Cabaret show; what you played stays credited.
A course failed in a term keeps that term from good standing.
A repeated year or an additional term past ${SIX} terms is billed to your Yale account.
Meetings missed ill stay excused on the record, and enough of them make an Incomplete, not a failed course.
A leave is refused while a request to repeat is being decided, and courses left on a leave are taken again when you’re back.
On an F-1, a repeat or an additional term extends the I-20 a year when it’s granted.
A repeated year or an additional term past ${SIX} terms is what bills tuition to the account.
The aid office grants tuition past ${SIX} terms only to a student who has had a medical leave.
Assigned hours excused ill or hurt are the hours conversion turns into grant aid.
Payments come out of your bank, and grant aid and refunds go into it.
Grant aid is a taxable scholarship, kept for the year’s tax return.
A hold at a term’s start means registering again before classes count you.
Assigned shifts kept or missed are part of the attendance the term’s review counts.
Friday’s pay goes into your bank as wages, and the equipment comes out of it.
A student on aid can convert assigned hours missed ill or hurt into grant aid.
Work-study wages are income on the year’s tax return.
A shift takes ${ESTIMATE.energy.shift} energy, and can hurt you at its work’s rate.
Registration does work-study’s I-9; without it, a shift is missed.
